findings.title: Possible NPE when the "Clients" resource-type resource does not exist
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` the fallback path assigns `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately passes it to `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource()` returns `null` in two reachable situations: (a) `supportsAuthorizationSchema()` is false (admin-permissions client exists but `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false), and (b) the realm's admin-permissions client was created before the `Clients` resource type was added to the schema, so no resource named "Clients" exists (there is no migration adding it). In both cases the policy store is queried with a null resource, which will throw a NullPointerException and turn every client-related admin REST call (view/manage/list clients) into an HTTP 500. The method should return `false` when the resource-type resource is missing.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission() returns the aggregate resource name instead of client ids
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission(scope)` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and collects `resource.getName()`. Two problems: (1) per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` are created with `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)` and never get a `type` set, so `findByType("Clients", ...)` never returns them — clients that have an individual permission are never reported; (2) the only resource actually typed "Clients" is the aggregate resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()`, whose name is the literal string "Clients", so the returned set can contain "Clients" as if it were a client id. Callers of `ClientPermissionEvaluator#getClientsWithPermission` (which in V1 returns internal client ids) therefore get either an empty set or a bogus id, so the permission-based filtering this method implements is broken.

findings.title: getResourceName() not extended for the new Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName()` only resolves names for the `Users` resource type. Now that `Clients` permissions can be created, policies with `resourceType=Clients` fall through to `return resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource()` (created with name + owner only, no display name) and for the aggregate "Clients" resource. As a result, representations of client permissions returned to the admin REST API/console will show a null resource name, whereas user permissions show the username or "All users". The Clients branch (client id/clientId and "All clients") is missing.

findings.title: No migration for realms whose admin-permissions client already exists
findings.body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so the new scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`) and the new aggregate `Clients` resource are only created for realms where admin permissions are enabled for the first time after this change. For any realm that already had the admin-permissions client created with the previous schema, these scopes/resources never get created, which means: `getOrCreateResource()` throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` when creating a Clients permission, `getScope()` throws `ModelValidationException` for the new scope names, and `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` hits the null `Clients` resource (see the NPE issue). Either an upgrade path that adds missing scopes/resource-type resources, or at least graceful handling, is needed.

findings.title: UnsupportedOperationException on reachable runtime/admin paths yields HTTP 500
findings.body: `canExchangeTo(...)`, `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)` and `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, but these are invoked from paths that are reachable while the V2 feature is enabled: the legacy token-exchange flow calls `AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo(...)` (producing a 500 on a token endpoint instead of a denial), and `ClientResource` exposes `GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions`, which calls `isPermissionsEnabled(client)` and is invoked by the admin console (again a 500 instead of a well-formed error). These should either deny/return a defined response for V2 or the calling endpoints should be guarded by the feature flag.

findings.title: Javadoc for void require* methods says they return true
findings.body: `requireView()` (line 95-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100-103) are documented as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}" / "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but both methods are `void` and, consistently with the other `require*` methods, throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` check fails. The Javadoc is misleading for anyone implementing or calling the interface and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false".

findings.title: New map-roles-client-scope scope is not covered by any test
findings.body: The PR adds three new scopes to the schema (`configure`, `map-roles-composite`, `map-roles-client-scope`) and the corresponding evaluation methods in `ClientPermissionsV2` (`canMapClientScopeRoles`). The new tests cover `manage`, `view`, `configure`, `map-roles` and `map-roles-composite`, but there is no test exercising `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` / `canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` (e.g. adding a client role to a client scope's scope mappings), so that scope's evaluation path is completely untested.

findings.title: Tests mutate shared realm state without cleanup, making them order-dependent
findings.body: `testManageOnlyOneClient` permanently renames `myclient` (`myclient.setName("somethingNew"); clientResource.update(myclient)`), removes a default client scope and re-adds it as an optional scope, and `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates the roles `myclient-role`/`myclient-subRole` on `myclient`. Unlike the policies created via `createUserPolicy(...)` (which register a `realm.cleanup()` hook) and unlike `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest` (which deletes the users it creates in `@AfterEach`), none of this state is reverted; only scope permissions are removed in `onAfter()`. Since the managed realm is shared by all tests in the class, later tests observe a changed default-client-scope list (e.g. `defaultClientScopes.get(1)` / `get(0)` indices) and left-over roles, which makes the suite order-dependent and prone to flaky failures.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports in the new class
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2` contains a private, never-called `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` method (copied from the V1 token-exchange logic, which this class explicitly does not support), an unused `logger` field, and unused imports (`org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, and the static `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE`). This dead code suggests token-exchange support that does not exist here and should be removed.
